 corpus, so which root was used is reported on stderr rather than inferred
 from the benchmark names.

candidate_9.doc_comments:
`[path(.foo[] | (.b0, ..., .b7) | .d | .d | .d | .d)] | length` over
 [`leading_iterate_comma_doc`] -- #2190's repro, and the one shape the
 groups above miss.

 The distinguishing feature is a **leading** bare iterate. #888 removed this
 exact O(n^2) for a *trailing* one by deferring it (`resolve_dynamic_indexes`'s
 `defer_trailing_iterate`), which is what `jq_write_path_path_array` above
 covers; a leading one is still enumerated to one resolved branch per
 element before the walk runs, so the branch count scales with the document.
 The comma is what forces the enumeration -- at width 1 the parenthesised
 group is an `Expr::Paren`, not an `Expr::Comma`, `needs_path_prepass` is
 false, and the whole shape collapses to a single branch.

 Before #2190 `builtin_path_on_owned` handed each of those branches a **deep
 clone of the whole document**, so the cost was `branches x nodes` and both
 factors grow with `elems` together: measured exponent ~1.98 (each doubling
 costing ~3.94x). The fix borrows the document instead, which should read
 ~1.0 here. Because `Throughput::Elements` is set, an exponent regression is
 visible directly in Criterion's ns/element column without eyeballing the
 raw timings.

 Wrapped in `length` so the timed *output* stays O(1) — this repo's own
 benchmarking discipline warns that a shape whose output grows with the
 input measures the renderer as much as the evaluator.

state.issue:
yq: stages before a metadata assignment are evaluated twice, so a side effect in an assignment RHS (`.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"`) fires twice

## Summary

When a pipe contains a #798 metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`), every earlier stage is evaluated twice: once by the write pass that works out which document the metadata write sees, and once by the real evaluation. A side effect inside such a stage therefore fires twice:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a = .a'
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2
b: 2
```

Reproduced on succinctly at `3a3e88140`. Real yq has no `debug` (its lexer rejects it), so this is only reachable through `--jq-extensions`, but the duplicated output is wrong on its own terms: the control case prints once.

## Mechanism

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs before evaluation. To make `.a = 2 | .b line_comment = (.a | tostring)` write `# 2` (as real yq does) it re-evaluates each stage preceding the last metadata write through `evaluate_input_quiet` and carries the first output forward as the document the next stage sees. `is_value_identity_stage` exempts a bare `debug`/`debug(msg)` *stage* precisely so its side effect isn't repeated, but a `debug` (or `stderr`, `input`, `halt_error`, ...) nested inside a stage's right-hand side is still re-run.

## Possible directions

- Detect a side-effecting builtin anywhere inside a stage that precedes a metadata write (a walk with `jq::walk::any_subexpr`, the way `count_meta_assigns` already does) and either refuse explicitly or fall back to resolving against the pristine document for that pipe.
- Or remove the re-evaluation entirely by applying the write *during* evaluation (`eval_meta_assign` recording `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local the runner drains), which is also the route #2705 needs. That makes each stage run exactly once.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the pipe-sequential resolution that introduces the second evaluation was part of that review's fixes.
- `input`/`inputs` would be worse than a duplicated line (they consume input), but they are not shape-preserving so the write pass never runs for a pipe that contains them at top level; only a nested use inside an assignment RHS could reach this.
